## The problem

`.github/workflows/test.yml:329-333` currently reads:

```yaml
  # Windows compatibility (epic 5664 S5). rebar is git- and path-heavy and the gate
  # runs only Linux + macOS; this sweeps Windows so a path-separator / temp-dir /
  # file-lock regression surfaces off the hot path. Non-blocking: Windows is not yet a
  # declared support target, so a genuine incompatibility is a visible finding, never a
  # red gate.
```

Under the operator's adoption of option (a) on `f850-674c-c89f-4b97`, **"Windows is not yet a
declared support target" is false.** The tree currently asserts the opposite of the decision, and
will keep asserting it for the whole life of this epic unless corrected now.

(The line range was `:340-344` when this ticket was written; re-checked against `origin/main`
`e510c64dbcb6`, the block sits at `:329-333`.)

## The original proving command was vacuous — this matters

This ticket was filed with `grep -n "not yet a declared support target" .github/workflows/test.yml`
as the proof. **That grep returns nothing on the UNCORRECTED tree**, so it cannot distinguish a
fixed file from a broken one. The falsified sentence is wrapped across two physical comment lines —
line 331 ends `Windows is not yet a` and line 332 begins `# declared support target,` — and a
single-line `grep` never sees the joined phrase. Verified:
`git show origin/main:.github/workflows/test.yml | grep -c "not yet a declared support target"` is
`0`.

Any check for this claim must therefore **join the comment lines and normalise whitespace before
matching**, or it is vacuously green. That applies to the regression test below as much as to the
manual proof.

## Why this is a separate, UNBLOCKED, first-landing task

This is the one child that is not blocked by S1. It changes no code and no job behaviour — the job
stays `continue-on-error: true` — so it can land immediately and costs nothing. Its whole value is
that it changes what a reader concludes from the red badge: from **"ignorable, nobody intends to fix
this"** to **"a known-incomplete declared support target being driven to green under epic
`simple-brotherly-peacock`"**.

That distinction is the entire signal-quality complaint of `f850`. Leaving it unrecorded for months
would reproduce the original defect under a new justification.

## Scope — what to change, and what NOT to change

**Do change:** the comment block. It must say Windows IS a declared support target, that the job is
temporarily non-voting because the epic is in flight, name the epic and the ADR, and state that the
`continue-on-error` removal is the epic's exit criterion.

**Also add:** a regression test that fails if the correction is reverted or over-applied, following
the anti-rot precedent in `tests/unit/test_probe_wired_into_ci.py`. Comments survive no structural
check, so the false-claim half is asserted against the file's joined, whitespace-normalised comment
text and the behavioural half against the parsed YAML document.

**Do NOT change:** `continue-on-error: true`, the `if:` schedule/dispatch condition, or anything in
`.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`. Flipping the job to gating now would redden every change
with 510 unrelated failures and wreck the `Verified` signal — that is S11's job, at the end, under
ADR 0114.

This change is additive and text-only: it edits a YAML comment and adds one test file. It touches no
data, no store and no job behaviour, so there is nothing to back up and nothing to roll back beyond
reverting the commit.

## Testing

```
uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/test_windows_support_target.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
uv run --no-sync pytest -k "workflow" -m "not integration and not external" -q -p no:cacheprovider
python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/test.yml'))"
grep -n "continue-on-error: true" .github/workflows/test.yml    # must still match sweep-windows
make lint && make typecheck
```

The new test's assertions are proven by mutation rather than assumed. Four mutations are applied to
a corrected tree and each must fail the intended test and no other: reintroduce the sentence on one
line; reintroduce `origin/main`'s **wrapped** block verbatim (the case a single-line grep misses);
delete `continue-on-error: true`; drop the ADR citation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The `sweep-windows` comment text, with its lines joined and whitespace normalised, contains no
      statement that Windows is not a support target. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_windows_support_target.py -k does_not_assert` passes, and that test
      fails when `origin/main`'s wrapped block is restored verbatim.
- [ ] The comment names the ADR, the epic and the promoting story, and states that removing
      `continue-on-error` is the exit criterion. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_windows_support_target.py -k cites` passes.
- [ ] The job's behaviour is unchanged — still `continue-on-error: true`, still restricted to
      `schedule` / `workflow_dispatch`. Proof:
      `pytest tests/unit/test_windows_support_target.py -k "non_voting or hot_path"` passes, and
      `git diff origin/main -- .github/workflows/test.yml` shows changes only within comment lines.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` is not modified. Proof:
      `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.
- [ ] The regression test detects a reintroduction **however the sentence wraps**, not only on one
      line. Proof: the four mutations above are run and their results recorded as a comment on this
      ticket, including the wrapped-restoration case.
- [ ] The repo gates are green. Proof: `make lint` and `make typecheck` both exit 0, with the
      complexity and mechanism ratchets reporting `new=0 increased=0`.
